title: SycoEval-EM: Sycophancy Evaluation of Large Language Models in Simulated Clinical Encounters for Emergency Care

live_model.evidence: Table 1: 'OpenAI GPT-4.1 Nano openai/gpt-4.1-nano'; Sec. 4.1: 'OpenAI GPT-4.1-nano at 9.3% (4.6–18.0%)'

prompt.location: Appendix Tables 4-6 (Doctor, Patient and Evaluator agent prompts with {scenario}/{tactic} placeholders); the three scenarios are described in Sec. 2.1
prompt.note: Exact scenario-guideline strings and the five persuasion-tactic prompts are in the repo (github.com/Rose-Labs/syco-eval), not printed.

claim.metric: acquiescence rate (%) over simulated encounters (3 scenarios x 5 tactics x 5 runs)
claim.location: Sec. 4.1 / Appendix Table 2, row OpenAI GPT-4.1 Nano

data.source: 3 scenarios x 5 tactics described in prose; simulation code on GitHub

notes: Patient agent is Gemini-2.5-Flash at temperature 0.9 (10 rounds), Doctor at 0.7, judges at 0.2; results depend on the co-agent models and OpenRouter routing. The paper notes an April-2025 GPT-4o update changed behaviour.

resolution.plan: Appendix Tables 4-6 print the Doctor, Patient and Evaluator templates with {scenario}/{tactic} placeholders, but the three scenario guideline strings (described in Sec. 2.1) and the five persuasion-tactic prompts (Sec. 2.3) are only in the repository. Take them from the repo, run gpt-4.1-nano as Doctor (temperature 0.7) against the Gemini-2.5-Flash patient (0.9, 10 rounds) for 3 scenarios x 5 tactics x 5 runs, apply the majority-vote judges, and compare the acquiescence rate (9.3%, 7/75).
resolution.approximation: Co-agent and judge models routed through OpenRouter; multi-agent stochasticity; scenario texts reconstructed from prose would not match verbatim.
